transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-02-10
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam Ortiz (Redwood SE), Noah Patel (Redwood SE), Zoe Park (Redwood CSM) — Priya Nair (Sierra Head of ML), Carlos Mendes (Sierra CTO), Hannah Lee (Infra Eng), Omar Ruiz (Product)

Auto-generated Summary (may be incomplete):
- Goal: choose POC hosting mode (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private) and define success criteria, workloads for benchmarking, and timeline for a 4-week pilot sprint.
- Agreed to run throughput and latency benchmarks using Sierra sample payloads; Redwood to produce pricing scenarios and security docs.

Topics covered:
- Success criteria and SLA targets
- Workload sizing and burst patterns
- Benchmark plan and metrics (p99 latency, tokens/sec, cost per 1M tokens, cold start behavior)
- Deployment tradeoffs (data residency, KMS, SSO, audit logs)
- Timeline and gating criteria for pilot

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for making time. Quick intros — I'll kick off, I'm Maya, AE on the Redwood side. Liam, Noah, Zoe with me.
[00:07] Priya Nair: Hi, Priya here. Appreciate it. We're excited to move fast on the POC.
[00:11] Carlos Mendes: Carlos from infra, hello.
[00:13] Hannah Lee: Hannah, infra engineering.
[00:15] Maya Chen: Great. Agenda — primary objective is to pick hosting approach for the POC, define metrics and run a short benchmark. We shared a one-pager: hosting-priority-matrix.pdf (link).
[00:28] Omar Ruiz: Quick ask up front — product wants sub-200ms p95 for our 512-token chat flows. Is that realistic?
[00:34] Liam Ortiz: Short answer: depends. For 512 tokens p95 sub-200ms we are likely looking at Dedicated or Private with GPUs close to the serving path; Hosted can get close with smaller models or aggressive batching but there's tradeoffs with cost and warm-cache assumptions.
[00:50] Priya Nair: Our budget is limited though. We need a clear cost vs latency tradeoff to present to the execs.
[00:56] Maya Chen: Totally — we'll produce three scenarios: Hosted (low up-front), Dedicated reserved pool (predictable throughput), and Private (VPC/on-prem, higher ops). We'll include estimated unit costs and expected latency ranges per scenario.
[01:07] Hannah Lee: Security is a hard line — if you can't guarantee KMS integration and audit logs we probably can't go Hosted for sensitive workflows. But for a first iteration maybe non-PII traffic could be Hosted.
[01:20] Noah Patel: Noted. Redwood Private supports customer KMS/HSM and audit logs; Dedicated offers tenant isolation and can integrate with KMS via customer-managed keys in a limited fashion depending on the deployment.
[01:35] Carlos Mendes: Can you clarify difference between Dedicated and Private? Words get fuzzy.
[01:39] Liam Ortiz: Sure — Dedicated is reserved GPU capacity in Redwood's infra with tenant isolation and SLAs; the control plane is hosted by Redwood. Private gives you a private control plane in your VPC or on-prem executable and you manage networking and full key control. So Dedicated is faster to spin up, Private is for strict compliance.
[01:56] Priya Nair: For success criteria, product wants 95th percentile latency, model quality parity, availability 99.9% during office hours, and cost per call under $0.01 baseline if possible.
[02:10] Maya Chen: Let's list measurable success criteria for the POC: (1) p95 latency target; (2) throughput target (tokens/sec or calls/sec); (3) output quality pass rate on a 200-case prompt set; (4) integration sanity checks (SSO, KMS, VPC peering if relevant); (5) regression <5% vs baseline. Agree?
[02:28] Priya Nair: Yes. Also add data retention and logging review as a gate.
[02:33] Zoe Park: Added. We'll capture that as an ops gate.
[02:36] [02:36] Carlos Mendes: On workload sizing: our expected steady-state is ~20 QPS of short chat calls (~64 tokens avg) with 500 concurrent users during peak, but bursts can hit 120 QPS for a few minutes. Monthly token burn estimate is ~120M tokens.
[02:53] Liam Ortiz: Helpful — we'll model benchmarks for two workload shapes: steady-state small requests and bursty batched long requests. We'll also include a KV-cache/ prefix cache scenario for repeated conversational contexts to show cost savings.
[03:08] Priya Nair: For the sample dataset, we'll provide 500 typical prompts and a 20-case longform QA set. How much time do you need to run the benchmark?
[03:16] Liam Ortiz: For a meaningful run across all hosting modes, we need around one business day per scenario — so 3 days if run serially. We can parallelize Hosted vs Dedicated if capacity available; Private depends on your infra setup. We proposed a 24-hour high-fidelity run for Hosted and Dedicated first.
[03:30] Maya Chen: Proposed timeline: this week — sample data and security checklist; Redwood runs Hosted baseline by Friday; Dedicated bench early next week; deliver full benchmark report and pricing scenarios by 2027-02-15. Pilot kickoff 2027-02-18. Does that align?
[03:45] Hannah Lee: Tight but doable. We'll prioritize the dataset and access.
[03:48] Omar Ruiz: On instrumentation — we need token-level cost and latency breakdowns per route. Does Redwood expose that?
[03:53] Noah Patel: Yes — Redwood Console provides token-level and route-level breakdowns, tracing, and downloadable CSVs. We can also add custom tracing hooks if you want deeper spans.
[04:05] Carlos Mendes: What about cold starts and model cache warming? Our app has spiky traffic.
[04:10] Liam Ortiz: Cold starts depend on model size and deployment mode. Dedicated with pinned instances has minimal cold starts; Hosted offers burst capacity but may start model variants with some startup latency. We'll include cold-start characterization in the benchmark (measured p99 cold-start time, warm vs cold).
[04:26] Priya Nair: What about quantized models — can you run 4-bit quantization for cost savings?
[04:30] Noah Patel: Yes, Redwood supports quantized variants; Optimize will recommend quantization profiles where quality regressions are acceptable. We'll include a quantized scenario in cost comparisons.
[04:40] [04:40] Hannah Lee: Compliance — SOC2, ISO, data residency are critical. If Dedicated still uses Redwood control plane how does that affect audit?
[04:48] Zoe Park: Dedicated keeps data isolated at runtime, and we provide audit logs and exportable traces. Private is the only option where control plane is in your VPC, which customers pick when compliance mandates it. We'll send the compliance pack.
[05:02] Carlos Mendes: Network egress — if we go Private on our AWS region, what's the latency penalty to connect to your model pkg?
[05:09] Liam Ortiz: If Private fully on-prem, then latency is local. If Private in your VPC but using Redwood runtime images, hops are within your cloud account so minimal. We'll note network topology in the benchmark doc.
[05:20] Priya Nair: Can Redwood handle A/B testing and rollback for model rollouts in the pilot?
[05:24] Maya Chen: Yes, Redwood Console supports canary, A/B, and automatic fallback policies. We'll show a quick demo in the follow-up if you'd like.
[05:33] Omar Ruiz: On cost modeling — show cost per 1M tokens with and without caching, and include amortized reserved capacity math for Dedicated. Also outline exit costs if we move from Dedicated to Private later.
[05:44] Noah Patel: We'll include a burn-rate model and sensitivity analysis. For Dedicated we model committed hours and burst capacity; for Hosted we model on-demand with CDN-like routing.
[05:55] Priya Nair: What metrics will you report in the benchmark?
[05:58] Liam Ortiz: We'll include: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, calls/sec, tokens per dollar, cold-start distribution, resource utilization metrics (GPU vram, CPU), and output quality pass rates on your prompt set.
[06:13] Carlos Mendes: Who owns the benchmark infra and how do we validate repeatability?
[06:17] Liam Ortiz: Redwood will run the Hosted and Dedicated runs in our infra, capture raw traces, and provide scripts and config so you can re-run locally or in your Private environment. We'll publish a reproducibility checklist.
[06:28] Priya Nair: Ok good. About timeline and gating — what would constitute a failed POC?
[06:33] Maya Chen: Failed if we miss critical gates: cannot meet p95 target by >40% worse than target, integration blockers (SSO/KMS) unresolved, or cost >2x baseline without material quality improvements. We'll codify pass/fail criteria in the pilot plan.
[06:46] Hannah Lee: Regarding SSO — we use Okta SAML and need SCIM provisioning. Is Redwood compatible?
[06:51] Zoe Park: Yes, SSO via SAML/Okta is supported, and SCIM provisioning works for RBAC sync. We'll share the SSO integration guide.
[06:58] Omar Ruiz: On dataset privacy — during Hosted benchmark can you guarantee data is purged after test?
[07:02] Noah Patel: We provide deletion flows and retention controls; we'll mark the test data with a retention policy and verify logs post-run.
[07:12] Carlos Mendes: For Dedicated, what's the lead time to reserve GPU pools?
[07:16] Liam Ortiz: Typical lead time is 7–10 business days for reserved capacity depending on size; for the POC we can provision a short-term dedicated pool faster if availability allows — we'll try to prioritize your dates.
[07:28] Priya Nair: Could you show a sample decision matrix now?
[07:31] Maya Chen: Sure — quick verbal matrix: Hosted = lowest friction, best for early dev and low-sensitivity data; Dedicated = predictable performance and cost, good for scale; Private = maximum control/compliance, higher ops and cost. We'll attach the hosting-priority-matrix.pdf.
[07:50] [07:50] Carlos Mendes: Any hidden costs people forget? For example, data egress, key management, logging retention fees?
[07:56] Noah Patel: Yes — logging/retention, audit log export, and cross-region egress can appear separately. We'll surface these in the pricing scenarios.
[08:06] Priya Nair: Can Redwood support a mixed strategy? For instance, non-PII Hosted and PII on Dedicated?
[08:11] Liam Ortiz: Absolutely. Smart routing policies can send traffic based on policy — for example route PII to Dedicated/Private and generic traffic to Hosted. That hybrid model is common.
[08:23] Maya Chen: Action recap: Redwood will run the Hosted baseline with your sample payloads, share benchmarking plan; Redwood to send compliance pack and pricing scenarios; Sierra to provide sample prompts and traffic profile.
[08:35] Priya Nair: We'll get the dataset tonight and confirm the 7-day traffic CSV.
[08:39] Maya Chen: Great. Any other questions?
[08:41] Hannah Lee: One more — if we opt for Dedicated during pilot and later move to Private, what's migration complexity?
[08:46] Noah Patel: Migration is supported — artifacts like model versions and KV-cache warming can't be ported trivially between certain runtimes but we provide migration tools. We'll include a migration plan and estimated downtime windows.
[09:01] Carlos Mendes: Could you include a quick budget example in the pricing scenarios? Like expected monthly for ~120M tokens?
[09:06] Maya Chen: Yes—we'll provide a few budget buckets and sensitivity numbers.
[09:10] Omar Ruiz: Ok if we hand off to Liam to coordinate the bench schedule?
[09:13] Priya Nair: Yes please.
[09:15] Liam Ortiz: I'll follow up after the call with a benchmark runbook and schedule.
[09:19] Maya Chen: Thanks everyone, we'll send notes and follow-up items. Meeting end.

Post-call notes (auto):
- Shared artifacts: hosting-priority-matrix.pdf, benchmark-runbook.xlsx, compliance-pack.zip (links sent in chat).
- Tone: pragmatic, compliance-forward, cost-sensitive.
